page.title: Best Phone With a Thermal Camera (2026): AGM X7 Pro vs Ulefone, Sonim, Blackview
page.h1: Best phone with a thermal camera
page.desc: Which phone with a built-in thermal camera to buy: real sensor resolution (256×192 vs 160×120), weight, battery and US carrier fit for AGM X7 Pro, Ulefone Armor 29 Pro Thermal, Sonim XP Pro Thermal and Blackview XPLORE 1 Pro.
page.intro:
Short answer. The best phone with a thermal camera for most US buyers is the AGM X7 Pro ({buy:agm-x7-pro}): a 256×192 thermal sensor (AGM lists the 512×384 upscaled output) at 25 fps, a -4 °F to 1,022 °F range, a 10,000 mAh battery and 375 g (13.2 oz) on the scale. That is 2.5× the thermal pixels of the 160×120 FLIR Lepton 3.5 inside the Sonim, Blackview and most Ulefone phones, and it costs about $200 less than the Ulefone Armor 29 Pro Thermal, which upscales the same 256×192 class of sensor and weighs 688 g (1.5 lb).

Carrier check first: the X7 Pro is an unlocked import with T-Mobile and AT&T bands (LTE 2/4/5/12/66, 5G n41/n77) but no Verizon band 13, and AGM does not list carrier certification. If you need a carrier-sold, FirstNet Ready phone, buy the Sonim XP Pro Thermal from AT&T instead and accept its lower-resolution Lepton sensor. If you only need to spot a hot breaker or a draft now and then, the Blackview XPLORE 1 Pro gives you a FLIR Lepton 3.5 for the least money, but at 640 g (1.4 lb).

Every phone here is a screening tool, not a radiometric instrument. Reviewers measured AGM's readings a few degrees high, and Ulefone's own spec is ±2 °C. Confirm anything that matters with a contact thermometer or a dedicated camera.

page.after:
What owners complain about

The same five problems come up in the EEVblog thermal-imaging thread, GSMArena comment pages, retailer reviews and the professional reviews of the AGM G3 Pro and Ulefone Armor series.

  • Inflated resolution. The most common gripe. AGM's 512×384 and Ulefone's 640×512 are upscaled from 256×192 sensors; Doogee's 1440×1080 figure is a fused photo. Compare native pixels: 256×192 beats the 160×120 Lepton 3.5, and nothing in a phone goes higher.
  • Carrier surprises. Imports list no carrier certification. Verizon users report being told their rugged import will not work, and AGM sells some US versions as T-Mobile-only. Check band 13 for Verizon, n71 for rural T-Mobile, and run the IMEI through your carrier's checker.
  • Readings a few degrees off. Notebookcheck found the G3 Pro read higher than an IR thermometer; Doogee owners report the same with no way to calibrate. Fine for finding a hot connection, not for documenting one.
  • Weight. Phones with 20,000 mAh batteries weigh 640 to 688 g (1.4 to 1.5 lb). Owners call them bricks. The AGM models stay at 375 g (13.2 oz); the Sonim at 267 g (9.4 oz).
  • Battery drain and support. The thermal app pulls battery fast on every model, and forum owners expect one or two software updates at most from Ulefone, Doogee and Blackview. AGM told Notebookcheck it plans five years of security patches for the G3 Pro.

Which one by need

  • Daily-carry thermal for trades and inspections: AGM X7 Pro ({buy:agm-x7-pro}). Highest native resolution available in a phone, 375 g, Android 16 and eSIM, for less than the Ulefone or the Sonim.
  • Same thermal with more storage and a work light: AGM G3 Pro ({buy:agm-g3-pro}). 12 GB and 512 GB, 18 W wireless charging and a 1,000-lumen floodlight, but no eSIM.
  • Carrier-sold phone on AT&T or FirstNet: Sonim XP Pro Thermal. The only thermal phone a US carrier sells, with a Snapdragon 7 Gen 3 and the lightest body here, but a 160×120 Lepton and a 5,000 mAh battery.
  • Biggest battery and brightest screen, weight no object: Ulefone Armor 29 Pro Thermal. 21,200 mAh, 120 W charging and a 2,200-nit AMOLED, with the same native thermal resolution as the AGM at 688 g and about $200 more.
  • Cheapest built-in FLIR: Blackview XPLORE 1 Pro. A Lepton 3.5 and 20,000 mAh for the least money, if you can live with 640 g.

Not recommended

  • Ulefone Armor 27T Pro+ and 25T Pro. Both carry 160×120 sensors at $449.99 to $579.99 on Ulefone's store (2026-11-06), more than the AGM X7 Pro costs for 2.5× the pixels.
  • Cat S62 Pro. Its maker, Bullitt, stopped operating; no updates or warranty support, and 4G only.
  • AGM Glory Pro. Out of stock on AGM's store and still on Android 11; owners report it worked only on T-Mobile.
  • Doogee Fire 6 Max. The native thermal resolution is not published, the phone weighs 529 g, and the 1440×1080 claim is a fused photo, not a thermal sensor.

notes: Query choice: 'best phone with thermal camera' and its variants return vendor blogs (Oukitel, Thermal Master), SEO listicles and spec databases; no page compares native sensor resolution, weight and US carrier fit. Reddit was unreachable (reddit.com blocked, two mirrors down), so complaint counts come from the EEVblog thread (30+ posts), GSMArena comment pages, desertcart/retailer owner reviews and six professional reviews. Pain-point counts: inflated or unclear thermal resolution 9; carrier/Verizon compatibility 6; readings a few degrees off with no calibration 4; weight 6; thermal app battery drain 3; few or no software updates 5; awkward report export 2. Segments and winners: (1) daily-carry thermal for trades and inspection: AGM X7 Pro, 256×192 native (highest in any phone), 375 g, $599, Android 16; (2) carrier-sold or FirstNet: Sonim XP Pro Thermal, $649.99 at AT&T today, Lepton 3.5 160×120, 267 g; (3) max battery/brightness: Ulefone Armor 29 Pro Thermal $799.99 today, 688 g, same 256×192 native per Ulefone's own GSMArena reply about the identical ThermoVue T2 module; (4) cheapest FLIR: Blackview XPLORE 1 Pro $359 today on store.blackview.hk, 640 g. Thermal resolution evidence: GSMchoice and iElectro spec tables list the X7 Pro sensor as 256×192 at 12 µm; AndroidGuys and Digital Camera World call the G3 Pro's 512×384 interpolated; Gizmochina gives 12 µm / 3.2 mm, consistent with a 256×192 core. Verification: AGM prices and availability (X7 Pro $599, G3 Pro $699, X7 $399, all in stock) read today via the store's search endpoint; the store's product endpoint and product pages returned HTTP 429 all session (also for Ulefone and Blackview product reads), so variant/version options and the AGM US policy page text could not be read today. Warranty (1 year) is from AGM's own blog and the en-ch policy page snippet; returns (15 days, defects only) from AGM's EU/CA refund pages read today; the EU terms page states 2 years, which is EU statutory, so I used 1 year for the US store. G3 Pro: two extra store handles at $629.10 and $643.08 (10%-off listings tied to the site banner) exist but could not be opened; record uses the canonical $699 listing. Not verified and kept off the page: AGM X7 Pro VoLTE certification on any US carrier; whether the AGM 'US T-Mobile only' variant wording applies to the X7 Pro (directly read only for the H6 Pro); Blackview US shipping terms; Doogee Fire 6 Max native thermal resolution. Amazon: amzcheck returned blocked/empty for every query, so no Amazon price comparison was possible; the AGM store is the only verified route. Codes: no Awin codes supplied; two site codes found apply to products not recorded (PAD P3, Note N2).
